---
title: "check-ball-neighborhoods.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a neighborhood written as an inequality
on a distance,
such as `\norm{\vx - \vx^*} < \delta` or `\abs{x - c} < \delta`.
The lab's notation rule writes such a condition
as membership in a ball,
`\vx \in \ball{\vx^*}{\delta}`
([psw#684](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/issues/684)).

The check reads math on the lines a pull request adds
to `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.md` files.
It flags a norm or absolute value of a difference
followed by `<`, `\lt`, `\le`, `\leq`, or `\leqslant`.
The norm may be written `\norm{...}`, `\abs{...}`, `\|...\|`, `|...|`,
`\lVert...\rVert`, or `\lvert...\rvert`,
with or without `\left`, `\right`, and sizing commands,
and may carry a subscript (`\norm{\vx - \vy}_2`).
Each finding reports the file, the line, the condition,
and the ball to write instead
(a closed ball for `\le`).

## What passes

The check does not flag:

- a norm with no difference inside, such as `\norm{\vw} \le t`,
  because the constrained form of a penalized fit
  is usually written that way on purpose;
- a comparison of two distances,
  such as the triangle inequality
  or a Lipschitz bound `\abs{f(x) - f(y)} \le L \abs{x - y}`,
  because the right-hand side holds a norm or absolute value;
- a difference whose first operand is a number,
  such as the step-size condition `\abs{1 - \steplen} < 1`;
- a `>` or `\ge` condition, which describes the complement of a ball;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following,
  `<!-- check-ball-neighborhoods: allow: <reason> -->`.
  The reason is required.
  The definition of the ball itself is the expected use.

## Why it blocks

Measured 2026-11-20 over lds, mds, pds, sds, mcs, and psw (whole tree):
49 hits, 45 of them neighborhoods
(epsilon-delta limits, continuity, local minimizers, Cauchy sequences).
Two of the other four are the ball's own definition,
which takes the allow comment.
The other two are a bound in a proof
and a radius check on a specific number.
Four exceptions in 49 hits are few enough to block on lines a pull request adds,
with the allow comment for the rest.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing pages never block,
and a page converts when someone edits it.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the norm inequalities a repository still carries.

Every run prints how many lines and files it examined.

## Limitations

- A condition split across lines is not found.
- A bare `|` pairs with the nearest `|` before it at the same group depth,
  so a conditioning bar inside the same group
  as an absolute value can mislead it.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `true`  | Fail the workflow when a neighborhood written as a norm inequality is found. Set `false` to warn only. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-ball-neighborhoods.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a neighborhood written as a norm inequality, such as
# `\norm{\vx - \vx^*} < \delta`, on lines a PR adds, and suggests membership in
# a ball, `\vx \in \ball{\vx^*}{\delta}`.
# Blocks by default; existing pages never block, since only added lines count.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check neighborhoods written as norm inequalities

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-ball-neighborhoods.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: false                             # warn instead of block (defaults to true)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-ball-neighborhoods.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-ball-neighborhoods.yml)
for the full caller stub.
